app.courseTitle: The course's name. Used on its own and inside other messages as {course}.
app.documentTitle: The browser tab's title. {page} is the page's name.
app.name: The site's name. Never translate it; keep it in Latin letters.
app.skipToContent: A link for keyboard users, shown only when it has focus.
certificates.offer.getCertificateFor: Screen readers only. {section} is the section's name, in English.
certificates.sheet.about: {course} is the course's name, in English. Keep Thinkerwell as it is.
certificates.sheet.finishedCourse: Printed straight after the learner's name, as one sentence. {count} lessons; {course} the course's name, in English.
certificates.sheet.finishedSection: Printed straight after the learner's name, as one sentence: "Amina finished the ... section of ...". {section} is the section's name and {course} the course's name, both in English. Word it so it follows a name.
certificates.sheet.signature: Under a line on the printed certificate where a teacher signs.
dev.localeOn: For developers only. Learners never see it. You can leave it in English. {locale} is a language code.
dev.rtlOn: For developers only. Learners never see it. You can leave it in English.
ds.actions.listenBar.slow: A reading speed. Very short: it sits in a small switch beside "Normal".
ds.actions.voiceButton.sayIt: The name of the speech-to-text button. Other messages use this name in quotes: keep them the same.
ds.actions.voiceRecorder.recording: Shown while recording. {time} is how long so far, like 1:05.
ds.chrome.logo.homeLabel: Screen readers only: the name of the logo link. Keep Thinkerwell as it is.
ds.chrome.progressRing.ariaLabel: Screen readers only. {value} done out of {max}.
ds.chrome.progressRing.valueLabel: Inside a small ring: {value} out of {max}, as numbers with a slash. Very short.
ds.chrome.siteHeader.switchLearner: Screen readers only. {name} is the current learner's name.
ds.chrome.stageDots.progressLabel: Screen readers only. {count} steps done out of 5.
ds.chrome.stagePath.doneSuffix: Screen readers only: read straight after a step's name (and its short description). Start with your language's separator, as the English starts with a comma.
ds.chrome.stagePath.stageDone: Screen readers only. {stage} is a step's name.
ds.content.definition.hearIt: A small button that says the English word aloud. Short.
ds.content.definition.meaningOf: Screen readers only: the name of a key word's pop-up. {word} is the English word.
ds.content.feedback.retryTitle: After a wrong answer. Gentle and encouraging: never "wrong" or "incorrect".
ds.content.option.correct: Beside a right answer. One word if you can.
ds.content.option.notQuite: Beside a wrong answer. Gentle: never "wrong" or "incorrect".
ds.content.reading.part: {n} of {total}: which part of the reading.
ds.course.journalEntry.lessonLine: {number} is a lesson number; {title} the lesson's title in English, or a step's name.
ds.course.journalEntry.saved: Under a journal entry. {date} is a short date, already written in your language.
ds.course.lessonRow.ariaLabelLesson: Screen readers only: a whole lesson row read as one. {number} lesson number, {title} its English title, {status} a status ("In progress."), {cta} the button's word ("Continue").
ds.course.lessonRow.ariaLabelLessonQuest: As ariaLabelLesson, followed by {question}, the lesson's English question.
ds.course.lessonRow.ariaLabelQuiz: Screen readers only. {title} is already written ("Section check: History & Human Stories"); {status} and {cta} as in ariaLabelLesson.
ds.course.lessonRow.cta.start: A lesson row's button word. Very short.
ds.course.scoreSummary.skillResult: {got} right out of {of} questions for one skill. Short.
ds.course.sectionHeader.eyebrowWithTotal: {number} is the section's number; {count} how many lessons it has.
ds.course.sectionName.history: A section's name, shown where a page has no name from the lessons. The lessons themselves keep their English section names.
header.language.button: The header's language switch, for screen readers: {language} is the language on screen, in its own name ("English", "Bahasa Indonesia").
header.language.title: Above the list of languages the header's switch opens. One word if you can.
header.lookAroundTitle: Shown while someone uses the site without saving anything.
lesson.minutes: How long a lesson takes. {min} and {max} are numbers of minutes, for example 30 and 50.
lesson.nextStep: {stage} is one of the step names (stages.read and the others).
lessonPlayer.complete.badgeProgress: {title} is the section's name (in English). {completed} lessons finished out of {count} in the section; the form is chosen by {count}.
lessonPlayer.complete.badgeSection: {number} is the section's number and {title} its name (in English).
lessonPlayer.complete.summary: {title} is the lesson's title, which stays in English. {message} is one or two sentences (in English after a finished lesson). Put them in the order your language needs; usually leave this as it is.
lessonPlayer.complete.title: {number} is the lesson's number.
lessonPlayer.read.backPart: A button back to part {n} of the reading. Short.
lessonPlayer.read.checkRetryNote: Next to the quick check: there is no limit on tries.
lessonPlayer.read.glossaryHelper: The key words in the English reading are coloured and underlined; tapping one shows its meaning.
lessonPlayer.read.levelSimpler: The easier of the two levels of the English lesson text. Short.
lessonPlayer.read.levelStandard: One of two levels of the English lesson text: the usual one. Short; it sits beside levelSimpler in one small switch.
lessonPlayer.read.listen: A button that reads the lesson aloud (in English). Short.
lessonPlayer.read.listenLabel: {n} is the part being read, {total} how many parts there are.
lessonPlayer.read.nextPart: A button. {n} is the number of the next part of the reading.
lessonPlayer.read.partLabel: {n} of {total}: which part of the reading this is.
lessonPlayer.sayIt.listening: Shown while speech is being turned into text. Learners speak English here.
lessonPlayer.shell.continueTo: A button. {stage} is the next step's name (stages.write and the others).
lessonPlayer.shell.saveError: Shown when the device couldn't save. Calm, not alarming.
lessonPlayer.shell.sublabelWatch: Under the Watch step. {minutes} is the video's length in minutes. Short.
lessonPlayer.sources.intro: Under "Sources" at the bottom of every lesson step. The websites are in English, so say so.
lessonPlayer.watch.readInstead: A button that shows the video's ideas as text. Other messages refer to it by name (lessonPlayer.watch.slowBody, pages.teacherGuide.videoOffline): use the same words there.
lessonPlayer.watch.slowBody: "Read instead" is the button's name (lessonPlayer.watch.readInstead): use the same words.
lessonPlayer.watch.videoInEnglish: Shown under the video only when the lessons are in the learner's language (they are translated, the videos aren't). "Read instead" is the button beside it (lessonPlayer.watch.readInstead); use the same words.
lessonPlayer.write.helperSaving: Learners write their answer in English (the course is English practice), so spelling means English spelling.
lessonPlayer.write.helperSavingSayIt: "Say it" is the name of the speech-to-text button (ds.actions.voiceButton.sayIt): use the same words.
lessonPlayer.write.modePlanShort: Phone-width version of modePlan: one short word if you can.
lessonPlayer.write.modeStartersShort: Phone-width version of modeStarters: one short word if you can.
lessonPlayer.write.modeWriteShort: Phone-width version of modeWrite: one short word if you can.
nav.home: Header link. Short: it sits in one row with four others.
nav.journal: Header link to the learner's own journal of writing. Short.
nav.label: Screen readers only: the name of the main menu.
notFound.title: The page someone asked for doesn't exist.
offline.offlineTitle: Shown at the top of every page while the device has no internet.
offline.updateAction: A button that restarts the site with the new version. Short.
pages.about.goal10Title: A UN Sustainable Development Goal: use the UN's official name in your language if there is one.
pages.about.goal16Title: A UN Sustainable Development Goal: use the UN's official name in your language if there is one.
pages.about.goal17Title: A UN Sustainable Development Goal: use the UN's official name in your language if there is one.
pages.about.goal4Title: A UN Sustainable Development Goal: use the UN's official name in your language if there is one.
pages.about.goalsNote: Needed wherever the UN goal icons appear: keep the meaning exact (no endorsement).
pages.about.justinName: A person's name: keep it as it is, or write it in your script.
pages.about.nickName: A person's name: keep it as it is, or write it in your script.
pages.about.missionBody: The team's approved mission statement. Translate it closely: keep every part, don't shorten it or add to it.
pages.allCertificates.labelSection: Screen readers only: the name of one certificate among several. {name} is a learner's name; {section} the section's name, in English.
pages.answerKey.question: {n} is a question number; {skill} a skill's name.
pages.classView.atStep: Under the lesson a learner is on. {stage} is a step's name (Read, Write, Speak, Watch, Reflect).
pages.classView.learnerAdded: Shown only when two learners share a name. {name} is a learner's name; {date} the day they were added, already written.
pages.classView.lesson: {number} is the lesson's number; {title} its title, in English.
pages.classView.lessonsOf: Lessons a learner has finished in one section, beside the section's name: {completed} out of {total}.
pages.codeCards.cardHow: Printed on each learner's card. {tile} is the home page tile's own words (pages.home.newLearnerTile), shown in quotation marks.
pages.codeCards.prefixHelper: HLP is an example code prefix (HELP for Refugees): keep it as it is.
pages.consentForm.formIntro: Printed for parents and guardians, in a respectful register (in Indonesian, "Anda"). {organisation} is the organisation's name, or a line to write it on.
pages.consentForm.orgBlank: Screen readers only: read out where the printed form has a line to write the organisation's name on.
pages.consentForm.pageOf: Printed at the top of each page of the consent form, which has two.
pages.consentForm.classQuestion: The parent's or guardian's first answer, with a Yes and a No box. A promise to families: translate it exactly.
pages.consentForm.studyQuestion: The parent's or guardian's second answer, with a Yes and a No box. A promise to families: translate it exactly.
pages.consentForm.signature: A parent who can't write presses a thumb in ink instead of signing.
pages.consentForm.learnerScript: Read aloud by staff to a learner aged about 10 to 17, in the learner's language. Speak to the learner as on learner pages (in Indonesian, "kamu"), simply and warmly. "We" is the organisation's staff and Thinkerwell.
pages.consentForm.learnerWins: A rule for staff, printed on the form. Keep it as firm as the English.
pages.consentForm.witnessBody: Signed by a staff member who read the form aloud. {language} is a line to write the language on, with the word "language" after it as a label.
pages.consentForm.languageBlank: Screen readers only: read out where the printed form has a line to write a language on.
pages.consentForm.questions: {organisation} is the organisation's name, or a line to write it on. Used while the team has no email address (src/app/contact.ts).
pages.consentForm.questionsEmail: {email} is the team's email address. Keep it as it is. Used instead of pages.consentForm.questions once the team has an address.
pages.course.lessonLabel: {number} is a lesson number; {section} the section's name, which stays in English.
pages.course.numberRange: A range of lesson numbers, for example 1–9. Use your language's usual way of writing a range.
pages.course.sectionCheckRowTitle: {title} is the section's name, in English.
pages.course.sidebarCount: Lessons finished out of the section's lessons, for example "3 of 9". Very short.
pages.credits.fontAtkinson: Keep the font's name and its authors' name as they are (they are names); translate only the words in brackets.
pages.credits.fontEczar: Keep the font's name and its authors' name as they are (they are names); translate only the words in brackets.
pages.credits.fontFunnel: Keep the font's name and its authors' name as they are (they are names); translate only the words in brackets.
pages.credits.fontVazirmatn: Keep the font's name and its authors' name as they are (they are names); translate only the words in brackets.
pages.credits.fontsBody: "SIL Open Font License 1.1" is the licence's name: keep it as it is.
pages.credits.fontsLicenceLink: "SIL Open Font License" is the licence's name: keep it as it is.
pages.credits.goalsStatement: The UN's own disclaimer for anyone using the goal icons (SDG guidelines). Use the UN's official wording in your language if it has one; otherwise translate it exactly.
pages.credits.goalsTitle: Use the UN's official name for the Sustainable Development Goals in your language if there is one.
pages.credits.lessonHeading: {number} is the lesson's number and {title} its title. Keep both.
pages.credits.softwareItem: {name} is a program's name and {licence} its licence's name; both stay in English. Keep the brackets or use your language's usual way of adding a note.
pages.credits.videoBy: {channel} is the name of a YouTube channel, which stays in English.
pages.educators.answerKeyLabel: Screen readers only. {section} is the section's name, in English.
pages.educators.codesBody: HLP-07 is an example code: keep it as it is.
pages.educators.feedbackBody: {email} is the team's email address, shown as a link. Keep it as it is.
pages.educators.teacherGuideLabel: Screen readers only. {number} is a lesson number.
pages.home.dashboard.greeting: {name} is the learner's name or nickname.
pages.home.dashboard.latestEntry: {stage} is a step's name (stages.write or stages.reflect); {number} a lesson number.
pages.home.dashboard.sectionCheckBody: {count} lessons in the section; {questions} questions in its check.
pages.home.dashboard.summaryInProgress: {count} lessons finished; {number} is the next lesson's number. The form is chosen by {count}.
pages.home.lookAround: A button for someone who wants to try the site without saving anything.
pages.home.newLearner.classCodePlacehold: HLP-07 is an example class code: keep it exactly as it is.
pages.home.newLearner.nameLabel: Learners may use a nickname: no real or full name is needed.
pages.home.newLearner.startsWithLesson: {number} is a lesson number and {title} its title, which stays in English.
pages.home.newLearner.submit: A button. The number 1 is the first lesson's number.
pages.home.remove.cancel: A button. {name} is a learner's name.
pages.home.remove.label: Screen readers only. {name} is a learner's name.
pages.home.tileAdded: Shown only when two learners share a name. {date} is the day the learner was added, already written in your language.
pages.home.tileMeta: Under a learner's name on their tile. {number} is a lesson number. Short.
pages.home.tileMetaAdded: {meta} is pages.home.tileMeta or pages.home.tileMetaNone, already translated; {date} is a date.
pages.home.title: The first thing learners see on a shared device. Friendly.
pages.journal.filterAll: One of three options in a small switch, beside filterWriting and filterReflections. Short.
pages.journal.groupLabel: {number} is a lesson number; {title} the lesson's title, in English.
pages.journal.pieceCount: {count} pieces of writing; {lessons} is pages.journal.lessonCount, already written ("3 lessons"). The form is chosen by {count}.
pages.lesson.title: The browser tab's title. {number} is the lesson number, {stage} a step's name.
pages.sectionCheck.factQuestions: {count} questions; {range} is a range of lesson numbers.
pages.sectionCheck.fromLesson: {number} is a lesson number; {question} the lesson's question, in English.
pages.sectionCheck.questionEyebrow: {n} is the question's number; {skill} one of the pages.sectionCheck.skill names.
pages.sectionCheck.reviewQuestion: {n} is a question number; {question} the question, in English.
pages.sectionCheck.scoreHeading: The learner's score: {score} right answers out of {total} questions.
pages.sectionCheck.title: {section} is the section's name, in English.
pages.settings.intro: The Settings page is for teachers and volunteers, not for learners.
pages.settings.language.help: Explains the language setting for the whole device. In a language whose lessons are translated too (Indonesian), say that the lessons show in it; otherwise say they stay in English.
pages.settings.listenVoice.automaticNow: {voice} is a voice's name as the device gives it (for example Daniel or Microsoft Hazel). It stays as it is.
pages.settings.listenVoice.nameWithLang: Used only when two voices share a name: {name} is the name as the device gives it, {lang} its language code (for example en-GB). Both stay as they are.
pages.settings.listenVoice.voiceFor.en: Labels the list of voices for lessons in English. Say the lessons are in English, not that they teach English.
pages.settings.listenVoice.voiceFor.id: Labels the list of voices for lessons in Indonesian. Say the lessons are in Indonesian, not that they teach Indonesian.
pages.settings.listenVoice.voiceFor.ms: Labels the list of voices for lessons in Malay. Say the lessons are in Malay, not that they teach Malay.
Menu and button names are the device's own: use the words the device shows in your language. Enhanced and Premium are how an iPad marks better voices.
pages.settings.listenVoice.better.androi: Menu and button names are the device's own: use the words the device shows in your language.
pages.settings.listenVoice.better.window: Menu and button names are the device's own: use the words the device shows in your language. English (United Kingdom) is a voice language as Windows names it.
pages.settings.listenVoice.better.chrome: Menu and button names are the device's own: use the words the device shows in your language.
pages.settings.sayIt.allowOnline: The name of a switch. pages.settings.sayIt.onlineOnly refers to it ("unless you allow that below").
pages.settings.transfer.load.added: {names} is a list of learners' names, already joined the way your language joins a list.
pages.settings.transfer.load.learnerNew: {name} is a learner's name; {work} is lessonsAndChecks, lessons, checks or noWork, already written.
pages.settings.transfer.load.lessonsAndC: {lessons} and {checks} are the lessons and checks messages, already written.
pages.settings.transfer.load.problems.no: Keep "thinkerwell" as it is: it is the start of the file's name.
pages.settings.transfer.save.learnerAdde: {name} is a learner's name; {date} the day they were added, already written.
pages.settings.transfer.save.saved: {file} is the file's name, which starts with "thinkerwell". It stays as it is.
pages.setup.homeScreen.android.step2: Button and menu names are the browser's own: use the words Chrome shows in your language.
pages.setup.homeScreen.android.step3: Button and menu names are the browser's own: use the words Chrome shows in your language.
pages.setup.homeScreen.apple.step2: Button and menu names are the browser's own: use the words Safari shows in your language.
pages.setup.homeScreen.apple.step3: Button and menu names are the browser's own: use the words Safari shows in your language.
pages.setup.homeScreen.desktop.step3: Button and menu names are the browser's own: use the words Chrome or Edge shows in your language.
pages.setup.homeScreen.thisDevice: {device} is one of the three kinds of device (pages.setup.homeScreen.apple.name, android.name, desktop.name).
pages.setup.homeScreen.why: {count} is a number of days: how long Safari keeps a website's saved work without a visit.
pages.setup.learners.how: Add a learner and I'm new here are the names of buttons: use the same words as those messages.
pages.setup.paperIntro: Printed at the top of the checklist. For educators and Set up this device are the names of a menu link and a page: use the same words as those messages.
pages.setup.speech.how: Say it and Check this device are names used in Settings: use the same words as those messages.
pages.setup.storage.how: Keep work safe is the button's name (pages.setup.storage.button). Allow is the browser's own word.
pages.setup.voice.how: Listen voice is the name of a part of Settings (pages.settings.listenVoice.title): use the same words.
pages.setup.voice.automatic: {voice} is a voice's name as the device gives it. It stays as it is.
pages.setup.voice.chosen: {voice} is a voice's name as the device gives it. It stays as it is.
pages.teacherGuide.planColumn: A table heading: a number of minutes. Very short.
pages.teacherGuide.sectionValue: {number} is the section's number and {title} its name, in English.
pages.teacherGuide.startHelp: A label followed by an English sentence starter.
pages.teacherTools.newTab: Screen readers only, after a link's name.
pages.teacherTools.why: A label followed by an English explanation, for teachers.
print.brand: At the top of printed pages. Keep Thinkerwell as it is.
print.optional: Put after a question on paper.
print.videoNote: {title} is the video's title and {channel} its channel, both in English.
print.writtenVersion: {title} is the video's title, in English.
routeError.body: Shown when something breaks. The learner's work is safe.
stages.read: The name of one of a lesson's five steps. Used alone (tabs, a list of steps) and inside other messages as {stage} ("Continue to {stage}", "Next step: {stage}"). Choose a form that works in both.
stages.reflect: A lesson step's name. See the note on stages.read.
stages.speak: A lesson step's name. See the note on stages.read.
stages.watch: A lesson step's name. See the note on stages.read.
stages.write: A lesson step's name. See the note on stages.read.
pages.pilotStudy.questions: A promise to families, printed on the consent form and the information sheet: translate it exactly, without softening or strengthening it. One of three lines after pages.pilotStudy.intro, which ends with "your child:".
pages.pilotStudy.writing: A promise to families, printed on the consent form and the information sheet: translate it exactly, without softening or strengthening it. One of three lines after pages.pilotStudy.intro.
pages.pilotStudy.faces: A promise to families, printed on the consent form and the information sheet: translate it exactly, without softening or strengthening it. One of three lines after pages.pilotStudy.intro. The sentence in quotation marks is one the learner reads (in Indonesian, "Aku ...").
pages.pilotStudy.site: A promise to families, printed on the consent form and the information sheet: translate it exactly, without softening or strengthening it. It must cover everything the pilot's measurement logs (docs/research/MEASUREMENT_PLAN.md, section 4), in plain words. "Quick checks" are the questions in each lesson's Read step; "the simpler reading" is the Simpler reading level; "read aloud" is Listen; "read instead" is the Watch step's written version.
pages.pilotStudy.notTest: A promise to families, printed on the consent form and the information sheet: translate it exactly, without softening or strengthening it.
pages.pilotStudy.keepCode: A promise to families, printed on the consent form and the information sheet: translate it exactly, without softening or strengthening it. {code} is an example code, HLP-01, kept on one line.
pages.pilotStudy.keepList: A promise to families, printed on the consent form and the information sheet: translate it exactly, without softening or strengthening it. {organisation} is the organisation's name, or a line to write it on.
pages.pilotStudy.keepNeverAsk: A promise to families, printed on the consent form and the information sheet: translate it exactly, without softening or strengthening it.
pages.pilotStudy.keepNoDocuments: A promise to families, printed on the consent form and the information sheet: translate it exactly, without softening or strengthening it.
pages.pilotStudy.keepNoPhotos: A promise to families, printed on the consent form and the information sheet: translate it exactly, without softening or strengthening it.
pages.pilotStudy.keepDevice: A promise to families, printed on the consent form and the information sheet: translate it exactly, without softening or strengthening it.
pages.pilotStudy.keepGroup: A promise to families, printed on the consent form and the information sheet: translate it exactly, without softening or strengthening it. {organisation} is the organisation's name, or a line to write it on.
pages.pilotStudy.keepDelete: A promise to families, printed on the consent form and the information sheet: translate it exactly, without softening or strengthening it.
pages.pilotStudy.keepVideo: A promise to families, printed on the consent form and the information sheet: translate it exactly, without softening or strengthening it. {readInstead} is the Watch step's button (lessonPlayer.watch.readInstead), shown in quotation marks.
pages.infoSheet.happenBody: Printed for parents and guardians. {start} and {end} are dates and {sessions} a number of sessions, as staff typed them, or lines to write them on. {organisation} is the organisation's name, or a line.
pages.infoSheet.questions: {contact} is a staff member's name and {organisation} the organisation's, as typed, or lines to write them on. Used while the team has no email address (src/app/contact.ts).
pages.infoSheet.questionsEmail: {email} is the team's email address. Keep it as it is. Used instead of pages.infoSheet.questions once the team has an address.
pages.infoSheet.whatBody: Printed for parents and guardians. Name the languages the course is offered in: English and Bahasa Indonesia.
pages.infoSheet.runBy: Names stay as they are. Honest about what Thinkerwell is: never call it a charity or a registered organisation.
pages.infoSheet.startBlank: Screen readers only: read out where the printed sheet has a line to write this on.
pages.infoSheet.endBlank: Screen readers only: read out where the printed sheet has a line to write this on.
pages.infoSheet.sessionsBlank: Screen readers only: read out where the printed sheet has a line to write this on.
pages.infoSheet.contactBlank: Screen readers only: read out where the printed sheet has a line to write this on.
pages.consentForm.pilotCode: Printed at the top of both pages of the consent form. {code} is a line for the organisation to write the learner's code on (like HLP-01).
pages.consentForm.codeBlank: Screen readers only: read out where the printed form has a line to write the learner's pilot code on.
pages.about.linkedin: The site's name, LinkedIn. Keep it as it is.
pages.about.linkedinLabel: Read aloud by screen readers for the LinkedIn link under a team member's name. {name} is the person's name.
app.mascotAlt: Alt text for the mascot picture on the home page and About, read by screen readers.
footer.linkedin: A link to Thinkerwell's LinkedIn Page, at the foot of every page. Keep the name LinkedIn.
seo.home.title: This page's title in search results and the browser tab. Keep "Thinkerwell" and the "|". The six page titles use capital letters on the main words, as approved.
seo.home.description: Shown under the title in search results and in link previews. One or two plain sentences; promise nothing the site doesn't do.
seo.about.title: This page's title in search results and the browser tab. Keep "Thinkerwell" and the "|". The six page titles use capital letters on the main words, as approved.
seo.about.description: Shown under the title in search results and in link previews. One or two plain sentences; promise nothing the site doesn't do.
seo.course.title: This page's title in search results and the browser tab. Keep "Thinkerwell" and the "|". The six page titles use capital letters on the main words, as approved.
seo.course.description: Shown under the title in search results and in link previews. One or two plain sentences; promise nothing the site doesn't do. {lessons} is the number of lessons.
seo.educators.title: This page's title in search results and the browser tab. Keep "Thinkerwell" and the "|". The six page titles use capital letters on the main words, as approved.
seo.educators.description: Shown under the title in search results and in link previews. One or two plain sentences; promise nothing the site doesn't do.
seo.organisations.title: This page's title in search results and the browser tab. Keep "Thinkerwell" and the "|". The six page titles use capital letters on the main words, as approved.
seo.organisations.description: Shown under the title in search results and in link previews. One or two plain sentences; promise nothing the site doesn't do.
seo.credits.title: This page's title in search results and the browser tab. Keep "Thinkerwell" and the "|". The six page titles use capital letters on the main words, as approved.
seo.credits.description: Shown under the title in search results and in link previews. One or two plain sentences; promise nothing the site doesn't do.
seo.lessonTitle: A lesson's title in search results and the browser tab. {title} is the lesson's own title (its question), in the lessons' language.
seo.lessonDescription: Shown under a lesson in search results. {course} is the course name and {goal} the lesson's learning goal, from the lesson file.
seo.imageAlt: Describes the picture that link previews show (public/social-card.png). Its words, "Thinkerwell: Exploring Our World", are in English on the picture.
digitalWorld.banner.title: On every Digital World page while the preview is on. Digital World is the course's working name: keep it in English.
digitalWorld.chart.bar: One bar in the chart's spoken name. {label} is from the lesson, in English; {value} a number.
digitalWorld.chart.figureLabel: Screen readers only: the chart's name. {measure} is what is counted and {bars} a list of "label: number", both in English from the lesson; {start} and {end} are numbers.
digitalWorld.claim.postFrom: {from} is a made-up website's name from the lesson, in English.
digitalWorld.compare.mostMistakes: Shown under "Correct". {group} is a group of people from the lesson, in English.
digitalWorld.compare.notMost: Shown under "Not quite yet". {group} is a group of people from the lesson, in English.
digitalWorld.map.guideLink: {title} is the lesson's title, in English.
digitalWorld.sort.mostPeople: Teacher guide. {group} is one of the activity's groups, in English.
digitalWorld.switch.goTo: {title} is the name of the course Exploring Our World, in the interface's language.
digitalWorld.trainModel.groupTitle: {label} is "Healthy" or "Sick", from the lesson, in English.
digitalWorld.trainModel.labelFor: Screen readers only. {description} describes a leaf, in English.
digitalWorld.trainModel.lookedLike: {label} is "Healthy" or "Sick", from the lesson, in English.
digitalWorld.trainModel.next: {title} is the next round's name, from the lesson, in English, or "Try it yourself".
digitalWorld.trainModel.takeOutFor: Screen readers only. {description} describes a leaf, in English.
siteVideo.captions: Under the video's title: the video has captions in English.
siteVideo.dataUse: {mb} is about how many megabytes the video downloads, a whole number.
siteVideo.explore.p1: siteVideo.explore.p1 to p6: what the video says, a paragraph each, shown as its written version. Keep the figures, names and places as they are.
siteVideo.explore.p4: "Social studies and beyond" is Thinkerwell's motto; translate it the same way here, in p6 and in siteVideo.session.p6. Exploring Our World is the course's name (app.courseTitle).
siteVideo.explore.p6: The first sentence is the mission on the About page, word for word (pages.about.missionBody): keep the two translations the same.
siteVideo.explore.sources: Where the video's figures come from. Keep the names and years.
siteVideo.explore.title: The video's name, and Thinkerwell's tagline. It speaks to learners.
siteVideo.inEnglish: Shown only when the page isn't in English. "Read instead" is the button's name (ds.content.video.readInsteadDefault).
siteVideo.playerOpened: Screen readers only, said when the video opens.
siteVideo.sameWords: Under a message saying why the video isn't showing (for example siteVideo.offlineTitle), above the written version.
siteVideo.session.p1: siteVideo.session.p1 to p6: what the video says, a paragraph each, shown as its written version. It speaks to teachers and staff.
siteVideo.session.p6: thinkerwell.app is the site's address: keep it as it is. "For educators" is the menu's name (nav.educators).
siteVideo.setup.p1: siteVideo.setup.p1 to p6: what the video says, a paragraph each, shown as its written version. It speaks to teachers and staff. "For educators" and "Set up this device" are the menu's and the page's names (nav.educators, pages.setup.title).
siteVideo.setup.p3: "Keep work safe" is the checklist's button (pages.setup.storage.button).
siteVideo.setup.p5: "Say it" and "Check this device" are Settings' own names (pages.settings.sayIt.title, pages.settings.sayIt.checkDevice).
siteVideo.setup.p6: "Social studies and beyond" is Thinkerwell's motto; translate it as in siteVideo.explore.p4.
